I have moved a LOT in my life / career. Usually when I land in a new place, I have use different tools from craigslist to meetup.com to find groups to play with in an effort to find a good reliable group that fit in with. It doesn't always work.

I feel like I've seen some of the worst examples of the bad player / dm stereotypes we've all heard about, but I surely can't be the only one with these experiences. I'll share one of my stories now and hopefully kick this off for responses, because I love hearing these stories.

I had just moved to Denver Colorado, and I knew literally nobody in the entire city. I hadn't played DnD in a long time, and I was a young college student who still held delusions of self-image, so I was a bit apprehensive to go searching for nerds as my first point of contact in the new place, but the nerd inside ME was not going to be denied.

I joined a group that played a bit outside of my normal region, but I was willing to make the drive because the DM seemed friendly and they were looking to start a completely fresh game and only needed one more person to complete the party. I spent all day rolling a half-elf ranger (this was a 4e game) and I showed up to the DM's house with my dice, my character sheets, a notepad, a 12 pack of beer, and a container of cheesy-puffs. (I was by far the youngest in the group at 23, the rest were in their late 30's or early 40's, and I thought I should show up with snacks and drinks to share, as that would be a good ice breaker and opening move to introduce myself to the group.)

That turned out to be a major error in judgement. I was the first player to show up, and I was greeted by the DM warmly at first, but once he saw what I had in my hands he frowned and began to fidget uncontrollably. He became extremely weird and I couldn't understand it, but he quickly ushered me into the house and directed me to the basement, where a folding table and some mats were already set up. He then went back upstairs to wait for the others.

I sat down there for about 25 minutes completely alone. I had heard other players show up, and they had stayed upstairs chatting with the DM and his wife. I was locked in the basement. When he went back upstairs he had shut the door behind him and I distinctly heard him turn the lock after he did.

I was already really weirded out, but I really wanted to play my new character I had spent all that time on, and chalked it up to nervousness all around and tried to stay positive. Eventually the rest of the group came downstairs. I had already opened a beer and I started to introduce myself, but each person that came down the stairs smiled at me and then I could visibly see their faces sink when they saw my beer, and after they saw it they would no longer make eye contact with me. We all sat down and began to play, and for a while it was fine. I was getting along with everyone, the DM was actually running a pretty high detail game and I started to enjoy myself and forgot about the initial weirdness of everything. I offered drinks and snacks, and was promptly declined. More for me, I thought.

Then it finally happened. The door upstairs opened, and everyone at the table with me immediately looked at me and panicked.

"HIDE THAT BEER!" the DM whispered aggressively. They had made no warnings or explinations up to this point, but I scrambled to oblige...

I was too slow. the DM's wife got to the bottom of the stairs with a tray of cookies as I was sliding a 12 pack under the table, and she lost her god fearing mind. She threw the cookie tray at our DM, started swearing and cursing me for bringing alcohol into her home, and I scrambled to gather my things and get the hell out of there as fast as I could. On my way out I noticed all the religious items all over the walls and put two and two together, but it was definitely a bizarre experience, to say the least.
